disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged (finance_domain, emerging_economy's revised position, pragmatist's revised position, and agentic_architect's/maximalist's concessions) against forcing actuals extraction into a single blocking job with comparatives loading: the period-lock gate on actuals is asymmetric to budget/forecast availability, and merging them would destroy post-close parallelisation. Extraction becomes an automated, lock-triggered pull, but the locked-period-actuals input (VAR-R-01) and a named human exception-review/reconciliation checkpoint survive, per KB-03 cutoff discipline and KB-05 error detection.

Kept as its own independently-triggered step rather than folded into actuals extraction, resolving the finance_domain/emerging_economy objection that a merge would wait comparatives loading on the close calendar for no reason. Automated loading is retained with an explicit version-identity confirmation sub-task (correct approved budget, correct forecast vintage), preserving VAR-R-02's required inputs and guarding against the recurring wrong-version failure mode several members flagged.

The arithmetic of price/volume/mix decomposition and FX isolation is automated, but the council majority (finance_domain, hitl_designer, pragmatist, accounting_standards, and maximalist's round-2 concession) rejected treating this as a judgment-free black box: the allocation and FX-fixing convention is itself a policy choice under KB-06/KB-07, and structural breaks can silently distort it. A recurring (per-period, not one-time) human validation checkpoint is retained, and the FX effect is reported as its own explicit line per KB-08, satisfying VAR-R-05 and VAR-R-06.

This was the council's central, unresolved conflict: maximalist initially argued the function could be folded invisibly into the automated engine, satisfying VAR-R-04 merely because an automated agent and the human manager are different actors. The majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, and agentic_architect's and maximalist's own round-2 concessions) held that this guts the control's purpose: a reviewer cannot test a selection decision made inside an opaque engine with no accountable human to interrogate. The synthesis sides with the majority -- materiality screening remains a separately named, separately performed step with a named analyst who sees the full population (not only flagged items), holds logged override authority distinct from threshold-parameter governance, and is a different actor from the VAR-07 reviewer. This satisfies VAR-R-03, VAR-R-04 and VAR-R-08 in substance, not merely in label.

The council split 2-2 (maximalist/agentic_architect for a labeled, human-confirmed AI draft; pragmatist/hitl_designer against any system-originated narrative) with accounting_standards declining to adjudicate beyond requiring the explanation of record to be traceably the budget holder's. The synthesis adopts the stricter line: no AI-authored draft enters the commentary step, because a controller must be able to defend to an auditor that the explanation was genuinely produced by the accountable owner, and labeled suggestions risk anchoring under deadline pressure with no way to detect it. The genuine, broadly-supported efficiency gain -- structured driver-tagged templates and automated escalation routing (finance_domain, emerging_economy) -- is retained instead.

Templated auto-population of the report is adopted (maximalist, pragmatist, agentic_architect), but finance_domain's and hitl_designer's objection holds: narrative synthesis -- judging commentary coherence and catching gaps -- is preparer-level judgment distinct from the manager's review and must not be collapsed into either pure automation or the review step itself, preserving the preparer/reviewer audit trail an audit committee would expect.

Every council member treated review and challenge as the workflow's non-negotiable human accountability checkpoint (VAR-R-07); no member proposed automating it. The one substantive refinement, adopted here per hitl_designer's and finance_domain's shared point, is that the reviewer must have access to the full variance population and the TS-04 exclusion/override log, not only the polished draft, so the actor separation required by VAR-R-04 has real rather than cosmetic teeth.

The council converged (maximalist's round-2 concession, agentic_architect, pragmatist, finance_domain) on splitting presentation from distribution: presentation involves live management Q&A a static report cannot answer and must stay human-led, while the mechanical publish/distribute action can be automated, gated on the manager's explicit sign-off, with a recall/reissue path. Per emerging_economy's non-negotiable, the automated distribution step treats offline/portable artifacts as co-equal to any portal, not a secondary afterthought.

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (data steward) with automated extraction system
steps.description: Locked-period actuals are pulled automatically from the closed ledger/sub-ledger on the period-lock event. A named FP&A analyst (data steward) confirms the extract ties to the locked period, reconciles control totals, and triages any extraction exceptions (missing entities, late-posted journals inside the lock). This step is independently triggered from comparatives loading so that cutoff discipline (KB-03) does not gate or be gated by unrelated data availability.
steps.name: Automated actuals extraction with data-steward exception review

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (data steward) with automated load system
steps.description: The approved budget version and latest forecast are pulled automatically from version-controlled repositories, triggered independently by a budget/forecast version-approval event rather than the period-lock event, preserving the parallelisation the close calendar depends on. The same or a paired data-steward analyst confirms version identity (correct approved budget, correct forecast vintage) before the dataset is released downstream.
steps.name: Automated comparatives load with version-identity confirmation

steps.actor: FP&A analyst with automated computation engine
steps.description: Price, volume and mix variances are computed by a calculation engine against actuals and comparatives on the same accounting basis, with FX effect isolated at constant currency and reported as its own explicit line rather than netted into mix. The engine logs, per run, the policy version and FX rate set applied. An accountable FP&A analyst validates, each period, that the policy and FX parameters loaded are current and that no structural break in the underlying population (new SKUs, reclassified cost centres, M&A-driven volume shifts) has silently distorted the computation; this is a recurring validation, not a one-time configuration sign-off.
steps.name: Automated variance computation with policy/FX validation and structural-break checkpoint
outputs: Variance dataset (FX effect reported as a separate line)

steps.actor: FP&A analyst (distinct from the FP&A manager in TS-07)
steps.description: A rules engine pre-flags variances against the dual percentage/absolute thresholds, but a named FP&A analyst, distinct from the FP&A manager performing review (TS-07), sees the full variance population -- not only the auto-flagged subset -- and confirms the selection list before it reaches budget holders. The analyst has explicit, logged authority to add back or stand down specific items for qualitative reasons (e.g., compliance-sensitive categories, cumulative small-item patterns, known control weaknesses), distinct from threshold-parameter governance, which is separately change-controlled. Every inclusion and exclusion is logged and visible to the downstream reviewer.
steps.name: Materiality threshold screening with analyst confirmation and override

steps.actor: Budget holders, supported by FP&A business partner routing
steps.description: Budget holders provide commentary on selected variances using a structured, driver-tagged template (price/volume/mix/FX/one-off/timing). Workflow tooling automates assignment, reminders, and SLA tracking, escalating non-response to the FP&A business partner or the budget holder's line manager. The channel is asynchronous and tolerant of low bandwidth (email/offline forms), not dependent on a live collaboration platform. The explanatory text itself originates from the accountable budget holder; no system-authored narrative is introduced as a starting draft, so attribution of the explanation of record is never ambiguous.
steps.name: Structured commentary collection with escalation routing

steps.description: A template auto-populates the standard report layout from the variance dataset and commentary feed, but an FP&A analyst compiles and finalises the draft: checking that commentary actually addresses the computed driver split, flagging implausible explanations, and surfacing any flagged item with no commentary received. This preserves a preparer/reviewer audit trail distinct from the FP&A manager's review in TS-07.
steps.name: System-assisted draft consolidation with analyst compilation and sign-off

steps.description: The FP&A manager reviews and challenges the draft report and its commentary, with access to the full variance population and the TS-04 exclusion/override log, not only the polished draft -- so the separation from selection has substantive, not merely nominal, teeth. The manager may send weak commentary or unexplained gaps back to TS-05/TS-06. This step remains human and distinct from whoever or whatever performed TS-04.
inputs: Exclusion and override log from TS-04
steps.name: Review and challenge

steps.description: The reviewed report is presented to management by the FP&A manager, who contextualises override decisions and fields live follow-up questions. Presentation and discussion remain a human-led activity, separated from the mechanical act of distribution.
steps.name: Present to management

steps.actor: Automated publishing system, triggered by FP&A manager sign-off
steps.description: Once the FP&A manager gives explicit sign-off, the report is published automatically to the management portal/dashboard and distributed via email, with a co-equal offline/portable artifact (PDF/downloadable file) issued alongside any dashboard link so recipients in low-connectivity settings receive the report itself, not an inaccessible link. Distribution is logged (what was sent, to whom, when) and reversible via a recall/reissue path if an error is caught post-distribution.
steps.name: Automated distribution and publication
outputs: Distributed variance report (portal and offline artifact)
